_what: Strategy desks for the Portfolio Manager. Same engine, same risk rules unless overridden, different candidate mandate, SEPARATE paper book and journal per desk — so the weekly review can attribute results to a setup class instead of to the blend. pm.py --desk <name> loads this file from $SCAN_DIR. The default desk 'swing' is the unfiltered book on the unsuffixed files and is what the Trade Desk board shows.
_rules: Every desk starts from the same $5,000 of paper capital, runs under the same account lock and paper lock, and is written back under the same revision/--check protocol. Desk books live at claude/paper-book-<desk>.json and journals at claude/pm-journal-<desk>.json. A desk with no candidates in its mandate simply reports that and manages its own holdings. A desk may name its day-trade / margin regime as rules.broker_policy (legacy_pdt | intraday_margin | cash_settled, see docs/PM.md section 4); unset, the book, engine-config.json and finally the default intraday_margin decide. A desk names its stop policy as rules.stop_policy (fixed_atr | chandelier | time_catastrophe, parameters in rules.stop_params — docs/PM.md 'Stops by desk type'); unset, fixed_atr. A desk with top-level "inactive": true is a TEMPLATE: pm.py --desk refuses it without --allow-inactive, no book is created for it, and the peer loader and paper mirror skip it. A desk with "kind": "options" is the paper options desk (D-02 / E27): pm.py --desk dispatches it to options_desk.run_slot under the same write protocol; its book carries `structures` (defined-risk spreads) instead of `positions`, and the house tally counts each structure as its beta-weighted-delta equity equivalent.

pullback.label: Pullback — mean-reversion entries inside an uptrend
pullback._thesis: Buy the dip in a name whose 200-day still defines an uptrend, RSI in the mean-reversion zone. Same ATR stop, same 3R target; the test is whether pullback entries outperform momentum entries on this scoring model.
pullback._note: Desk being retired (E-K07): a mean-reversion mandate under a 1.5x ATR stop sells into the drawdown it was built to hold through. Left on fixed_atr, unchanged, until the book is closed out.

momentum.label: Momentum — trend continuation only
momentum._thesis: Only names above both moving averages with the 50 over the 200 and RSI showing healthy strength, not exhaustion. Same risk rules; the test is whether trend continuation beats mean reversion.
momentum._note: Unchanged today. E-K07 proposes chandelier here — initial 2.5x ATR, 3x ATR trail under the highest close, 40-session time stop below 1R (Han, Zhou & Zhu 2016; Kaminski & Lo 2014) — once the harness shows it on this book's own trades. Switch by setting rules.stop_policy to "chandelier"; open positions keep the policy they were opened under.

rotation.label: Rotation — sector ETF momentum, monthly (E26) — INACTIVE TEMPLATE
rotation._cadence: Monthly: rank the sector ETF universe on 12-1 month momentum at the first slot of the month, hold the top ranks for ~25 sessions, rotate. The four daily slots only manage holdings between rebalances.
rotation._thesis: Cross-sectional sector momentum in liquid ETFs (E26). No tight stop — a 3.5x ATR catastrophe stop and the 25-session time stop are the only exits; the rank IS the exit. The `universe: sector-etfs` filter is a placeholder: the scan does not carry that universe yet, so this desk has no candidates and no book until it does.
rotation._note: Template only (E26). No book exists; pm.py refuses --desk rotation without --allow-inactive. Activate by removing `inactive`, creating the two project docs and adding the desk to runner/slots.json.

orb.label: ORB — opening-range breakout, intraday (E24) — INACTIVE TEMPLATE
orb._thesis: Opening-range breakout (E24): enter on a break of the first bar's range in the direction of the gap, stop at 10% of ATR (the paper's stop, implemented as chandelier k_init 0.1), flatten at the close — never held overnight. Needs intraday bars and an entry slot the engine does not have yet.
orb._note: Template only (E24). No book exists; pm.py refuses --desk orb without --allow-inactive. `flatten_at_close` closes every position at the power-hour slot; intraday_margin is required because every trade is a day trade.

options.label: Options — XSP/SPY put credit spreads, paper (E27) — INACTIVE TEMPLATE
options._thesis: E27, plan §6 / Appendix H §2, §7. XSP (fallback SPY) put credit spreads, 30–45 DTE, short strike nearest 20Δ, $5 wide. Premium at risk per structure ≤ 8% of desk equity ($400 on $5k: width×100 − credit×100); total defined risk ≤ 40%; ≤ 5 concurrent, ≤ 2 per sector; never on an underlying a stock desk holds. Exit at 50% of max profit or 21 DTE, whichever first; defensive close when spot trades under the short strike. No new short vol when VIX > VIX3M, VIX > 30, or SPY GEX < 0 (GEX from the chain snapshot; skipped and logged when the chain carries no gamma/OI). Portfolio limits: β-weighted delta within ±0.5% of house NAV per 1% SPY move, net short vega ≤ 0.5% of desk equity per vol point, theta ≤ 0.3%/day. Paper fills at the spread mid − $0.02/leg, legs with bid = 0 or spread/mid > 10% refused; fees $0.04/contract regulatory + $0.35 index ($0 equity commission). Marked every slot from chain mids; stress replay weekly (2024-08-05, 2025-04-07/08) by Black–Scholes. Reviewed at 60 sessions against the Cboe PUT benchmark's risk profile. The short-vol sleeve is a higher-Sharpe form of equity beta, not diversification — the house tally counts it as the hidden long it is.
options._note: Template only (D-02). No book exists; pm.py refuses --desk options without --allow-inactive. Activate by removing `inactive`, creating the two project docs (python3 options_desk.py --init-book paper_book_options.json for the seed), adding the desk to runner/slots.json, and staging option_chains.json (XSP/SPY puts) and vix.json ({vix, vix3m}) with every PM slot. Shadow fills do not apply — the paper fill is the conservative model. The dead-man's switch stamps no stop on a spread: defined risk bounds it.
